Five code locations in openmrs-module-webservices.rest call `savePatientProgram` directly. All of them are in the REST resource layer, so a behaviour change in openmrs-core could affect them.

1. **`ProgramEnrollmentResource1_8.save`** (`save` method, lines 92–94): returns the result of `savePatientProgram` as the enrollment's saved delegate. This is the main enrollment create/update path.
2. **`PatientStateResource1_8.save`** (`save` method, lines 112–117): adds a new state to the parent `PatientProgram`, then saves the parent. Any change to how states are persisted would hit this path.
3. **`PatientStateResource1_8.delete`** (`delete` method, lines 71–83): voids the last state on the patient program, then saves it. Its result depends on how `savePatientProgram` handles voided states.
4. **`PatientProgramAttributeResource2_2.save`** (`save` method, lines 74–88): adds the attribute to the enrollment if it is new, then saves the parent `PatientProgram`.
5. **`PatientProgramAttributeResource2_2.delete`** (`delete` method, lines 61–66): soft-deletes the attribute, then saves the parent `PatientProgram`.

The first two are direct `Context.getProgramWorkflowService()` calls. The last two use `Context.getService(ProgramWorkflowService.class)`. I searched only for the literal symbol name in this repository, so a wrapper that calls `savePatientProgram` indirectly would not appear here. I did not search openmrs-core itself to confirm the method's current behaviour.
